chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the likeness of Abū Ṭālib is the likeness of the Companions of the Cave: they concealed faith and outwardly showed shirk, so Allah gave them their reward twice.

key_terms.أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Abū Ṭālib, the uncle of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.أَصْحَابِ الْكَهْفِ: the Companions of the Cave, cited as a parallel example
key_terms.مَثَلَ: likeness or parable used for comparison

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describe the faith of Abū Ṭālib?
ai.summary: This hadith compares Abū Ṭālib to the Companions of the Cave, presenting him as one who concealed iman while outwardly displaying shirk under particular circumstances. It emphasizes that Allah rewarded such concealment undertaken in that context with a doubled recompense.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘An example of Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> is a example of the Companions of the Cave (As’haab Al-Kahf). They were secretive of the Eman and they manifested the polytheism, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Gave them the Recompense twice’.
